messages:
alex: Nightdash fired an alert ~00:15 UTC: p95 latency for the streaming endpoint jumped ~18% vs baseline. linking graphs: https://nightdash.internal/r/streams/3685
chen: saw it, digging into the nightly prober traces now. initial suspicion: kernel-selector path changed after yesterday's merge (PR #4321).
katy: @chen can you confirm whether KV hit rate moved? that would explain longer exec paths and extra kernel fallbacks.
chen: kv hit rate dropped ~6pp on the affected cluster (eu-west-1-gpupool). also seeing more frequent kernel fallback to the slower attention kernel in the flame graphs. attaching quick snippet:
```
flamegraph excerpt:
kernel_selector::score_compute ~45%
kv_cache::lookup ~12%
attention_slow_kernel ~18%
```
sam: PR #4321 was the batching+selector refactor, right? it changed the selection epsilon and added a cold-prefetch hint.
marie: yup that one. we intended it to prefer cheaper kernels for short sequences; maybe the heuristic is mis-classifying more requests as long-ish and forcing the slower kernel.
alex: CI perf runner didn't catch this because unit workload distribution in CI is skewed to short sequences. prober uses a more realistic mix at night which is why this surfaced in Nightdash.
katy: any obvious commits in that PR that could cause a kv eviction pattern? I remember there was a change to the prefetch window size.
chen: looks like prefetch window increased from 4->8 in the selector patch (file: runtime/prefetch/heuristics.rs). that could increase KV pressure and evictions, dropping hit rate.
sam: can we bisect to the exact commit? I can start a local git bisect on the release branch.
alex: please do — bisect with the nightly prober profile if possible. also file a quick rollback PR if bisect points to the selector change. we want to avoid a broad rollout blocker.
sam: starting `git bisect start --good v1.9.2 --bad HEAD` now. will run the prober job locally against each mid commit, ~10-12 steps expected.
infra-bot: perf-prober job queued (id: prober-3685-77). will post results when done.
marie: thanks. quick idea: add a temporary guard in kernel selector to cap prefetch window to 4 for dedicated pools until we understand impact. that would be a small patch to test.
katy: +1 for a small guard. easier to ship and test faster than a full revert.
chen: prober result from step 4 just finished: p95 back to baseline when prefetch capped at 4. that strongly implicates the prefetch expansion.
sam: bisect finished: first-bad commit is 9d4f2b7 (PR #4321, selector: increase prefetch window).
alex: ok. two action items: (1) emergency patch: add runtime flag to cap prefetch to 4 and ship to nightly clusters; (2) prepare full revert PR for the selector heuristic while we investigate deeper. who wants (1)?
katy: I can open the small patch and test quickly. will target canary pool first.
marie: I'll start the revert PR and add a thorough repro test in prober config to prevent regressions.
sam: once katy has the patch, let's run the prober and watch Nightdash for delta. also add a profiling run to capture kernel selection counts.
chen: note: we should also add an integration test that exercises mixed-sequence distributions for the CI perf runner. CI being skewed was the blind spot.
alex: agreed, add that to the revert PR checklist.
katy: opened patch PR #4360 (cap prefetch=4) and pushed to canary. CI green. deploying to canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary (deployment id: d-7782) by katy.
infra-bot: canary prober run started (job: prober-3685-canary-1).
chen: early canary prober result: p95 back within 2% of baseline, kv hit restored to previous level. flamegraph shows attention_slow_kernel drops back to ~6%.
alex: excellent. please proceed with a staged roll if canary remains healthy for 1h. also marie, ping when revert PR is ready.
marie: revert PR #4361 opened, includes added prober test and CI perf variant. assigning @sam and @chen for review.
sam: reviewing now, left small comment on the test harness.
katy: will monitor Nightdash and set an alert on kernel_selector fallback rate to catch re-introductions.
alex: after revert merges, we should run a focused performance QA run across regions and add a canary gate in the rollout pipeline to block if p95 delta >5%.
marie: noted. I'll update the rollout policy in the console and put the selector refactor back on the perf roadmap for a safer follow-up.
alex: thanks everyone. summary: nightly alert -> bisect -> culprit = prefetch window increase in selector patch -> temporary cap shipped to canary -> canary looks good -> revert PR + CI test added. closing thread when revert merged and rollout policy updated. :thumbsup:
